title: Minimum Window Substring
summary: Return the shortest contiguous piece of s that contains all the required letters from t.

contractDetails.constraints: Each string has 1–100,000 English letters, with case significant. The shortest qualifying window is unique when it exists.

statement: Return the shortest contiguous piece of s that contains all the required letters from t. A letter appearing twice in t must appear at least twice in the chosen piece. Use an empty string when no piece qualifies.

examples.explanation: The final three letters meet the counts and no shorter window can.
Uppercase K cannot replace the missing lowercase k.
The closest qualifying d and c enclose Y.

constraints: Each string has 1–100,000 English letters, with case significant. The shortest qualifying window is unique when it exists.
hints: Conceptual: A window qualifies only when it meets every letter's required count.
Directional: Expand the right edge until the window covers the requirements, then try to shorten it.
Implementation: When coverage is complete, save the best interval and shrink from the left until a required count drops below its target.
complexityAnalysis: O(|s| + |t|) time and O(1) auxiliary space for the fixed alphabet, excluding the returned substring. Each edge moves forward only.
